next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-running espionage group with many names
next.in_short: Known as Emissary Panda, APT27 and LuckyMouse, among other names. Vendors and a German agency report data theft from industry and government, using watering holes, unpatched servers and backdoors such as PlugX and HyperBro.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists Threat Group-3390 under many names: Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Dell SecureWorks researchers designated the group Threat Group 3390 and nicknamed it Emissary Panda. The group is believed to be based in China.
Symantec's Threat Hunter Team writes about Budworm, which it lists as also known as LuckyMouse, Emissary Panda and APT27. Symantec says the group is believed to have been active since at least 2013.
Germany's Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) describes APT27, also known as Emissary Panda, as a Chinese cyberespionage group.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence says Linen Typhoon, a name the catalogue gives for this group, has focused on stealing intellectual property since 2012.

Dell SecureWorks reported that most targets were in the automotive, electronic, aerospace, energy and pharmaceutical industries. At least 50 organizations in the US and the United Kingdom had data stolen.
The same report lists defense contractors, colleges and universities, law firms and political organizations among the targets.
Symantec says Budworm often focuses on government, technology and defense organizations. In August 2023 it hit a Middle Eastern telecommunications organization and an Asian government.
The BfV says attacks on German companies have been taking place since at least March 2021.
A Malpedia entry says the HyperBro remote access tool has been observed targeting primarily the gambling industry, though it has been seen elsewhere.
Dell SecureWorks said the group broke into networks largely through watering hole attacks launched from over 100 compromised legitimate websites.
According to that report, no zero-days were used. The group relied on old vulnerabilities, including CVE-2011-3544 and CVE-2010-0738, and used the PlugX remote access tool.
The BfV says the attackers got in through unpatched, internet-exposed servers, using flaws in Microsoft Exchange and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus. The final payload was HyperBro.

Symantec says Budworm ran its SysUpdate backdoor by DLL sideloading. It also used living-off-the-land tools and public tools such as AdFind, SecretsDump and PasswordDumper to map networks and dump credentials.
The Malpedia entry says HyperBro typically has three or more components, including a genuine loader and an encrypted, compressed payload.
One analyst's blog post says the Redosdru downloader is commonly associated with APT27/Iron Tiger.
The catalogue's tool list for the group includes PlugX, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, China Chopper, HyperBro, SysUpdate and Impacket.
Dell SecureWorks researchers unveiled the group at the Black Hat conference. The article was published on 5 August 2015.
In January 2023 the BfV warned of repeated attacks on German companies. It said it could not rule out attempts to reach customers or service providers through supply chain attacks.
Symantec reports that the August 2023 attacks used an updated SysUpdate variant. It says only credential harvesting was seen on infected machines, and the activity may have been stopped early.
In July 2025 Microsoft said Linen Typhoon and Violet Typhoon were exploiting on-premises SharePoint vulnerabilities, including CVE-2025-49706 and CVE-2025-49704.
Patch internet-facing servers quickly, and keep watch for unexpected DLLs loaded by trusted programs.
